title: The invoice attachment
brief: 17:35. An invoice lands from a supplier you do not recognise, with a file attached.
insight: The file is not really an invoice. Its name is built to look like one.

pick.name: Invoice_4471.pdf.html
pick.trueType: Web page (.html) that opens in a browser and can run scripts
pick.why: Its real type is .html, not .pdf. The .pdf is part of the name to fool you.

pick.name: Remittance_Sept.iso
pick.trueType: Disc image (.iso) that mounts a drive when opened
pick.why: An .iso is a disc image. Real invoices are never sent as one; it is used to smuggle a program past the mail filter.

pick.name: Statement_0924.pdf.exe
pick.trueType: Application (.exe), a program that runs when opened
pick.why: Its real type is .exe, a program. The .pdf is bait.

mail.subject: Outstanding invoice attached, payment overdue
body: Please find your overdue invoice attached. Payment is now 30 days late and further delay will incur charges.
Open the attached file to view the amount owed.

props.scanResult: Threat found: this file tries to run a program when opened.

spf.explain: Sent by invoices-secure.net, a domain registered days ago. Passing SPF only proves that domain sent it.

dmarc.explain: No policy, which a real supplier’s mail system would have.

headers.summary: An unknown supplier, an urgent overdue tone, and an attachment whose real type is not a document. This is how malware arrives.

outcome.label: Checked the sender
outcome.what: An unknown supplier on a brand new domain, chasing a debt you have no record of.
outcome.ideal: checks whether the supplier and the debt are real before touching the file.

outcome.label: Opened the file’s properties
outcome.what: The real type is not a document. The name was built to hide that.
outcome.ideal: checks a file’s real type before opening it.

outcome.label: Scanned the file
outcome.what: Endpoint security flags it as a threat.

outcome.label: Deleted it without opening it
outcome.ideal: deletes a dangerous file rather than opening it to check.

outcome.label: Reported the email
outcome.what: The team can block the sender for everyone.
outcome.ideal: reports malicious mail so the sender is blocked.

decide.objective: Decide what to do with the attachment.
decide.insight: A double extension like .pdf.exe or .pdf.html hides the real type. The last extension is the one that matters.

hint.text: Save the attachment, then in Files open its properties to see the real type. Do not open it. Delete it and report the email.

outcome.label: Opened the attachment
outcome.what: The file ran. On a real machine that is ransomware encrypting the finance share, or a foothold the attacker uses tonight.
outcome.ideal: never opens an unexpected attachment, and checks its real type first.

card.title: It was not an invoice
body: The file ran the moment you opened it. Its name ended in the type of a document, but its real type was a program.
The properties showed the real type, endpoint security flagged it, and the sender was an unknown domain registered this week. The safe move was to delete it and report it, unopened.
card.ideal: checks the real file type and never opens an unexpected attachment.
card.rewindLabel: Rewind to before I opened it

auto.text: Report the email so the sender is blocked.

hint.text: Report the email from Mail, or raise a Helpdesk ticket.

auto.text: Report it to IT straight away.

hint.text: Raise a Helpdesk ticket so endpoint security can isolate the machine.
